newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai Alphatec Group hard hit by bearish market.
newsitem.headline: Thai Alphatec Group hard hit by bearish market.

text.p: Thailand's economic slowdown and bearish stock market have marked up a new casualty -- the country's biggest electronics company, Alphatec Group.
The latest blow came on Thursday when U.S.-based Texas Instuments Inc terminated two joint ventures with the group, citing difficult economic conditions in Thailand.
Texas said Thailand's problems had hit the ability of Alphatec's major shareholder and chairman Charn Uswachoke to raise finance.
Alphatec Group executives said they were negotiating with various potential business partners for loans or to get them to invest in the two projects in which Texas Instruments used to have a stake.
But analysts blamed Charn's lack of success so far on a lack of confidence in the Thai economy, a difficult market situation and to certain extent, the nature of the business itself.
They said the government must step in to help the cash-strapped company. Otherwise the country's attempt to move up the technology ladder to replace labour-intensive exports could be at stake.
"If the Alphatec Group collapses, it will shake foreign investors' confidence because the company's name is synonymous to Thailand's electronics industry," a foreign analyst said.

"In other Asian countries which are at the forefront of the electronics industry, such as Singapore, South Korea and Taiwan, the government provided substantial support to jump-start the industry," he said.
The group has already been struggling to find $550 million or more to finish the country's first $850 million silicon-chip foundry run by Submicron Technology Plc.

When Submicron announced its funding plans in 1995, an initial public offering of 90 million shares was a major part of them. Officials had said they expected to raise as much as nine billion baht ($346 million) from the float.

But because the project was new to Thailand, it took authorities a long time to approve the IPO. By the time the Securities and Exchange Commission gave the green light for the IPO last year, the market had already gone from boom to bust.
The SET index ended on Friday at 605.43 points -- a far cry from a high of more than 1,400 in February 1996.
With the withdrawal of Texas Instruments from the joint ventures, Alphatec Group will need to find $25 million to buy Texas's shares in the joint ventures.
The company will also have to reserve $45 million baht for possible put options of its Euroconvertible bond this July, according to analysts.
One possibility would be to have the government take a stake.
Charn said on Friday the group hoped the government would invest up to $70 million in the group's two major projects.
"Alphatec Group's projects are greenfield projects and very capital-intensive. Investors tend to have reservations on such projects," said an analyst from Securities One.
"If the government threw its weight behind the group, it would make it much easier to raise the funds," he added. ($1 - 26 baht)
